newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly lower, but marks and yen are expected to gravitate to the upside as the selloff in U.S. T-bonds and U.S. stocks may drag down the dollar overnight, traders said.

"The fundamentals that have helped the dollar have not changed in the last week, but the selloff in bonds and stocks has been disruptive," Bob Lynch, currency strategist at Paribas Capital Markets, said.
September yen and marks remained on the defensive all day, despite U.S. T-bonds' late reversal to the downside and the weakness in the U.S. stock market.
Traders said the prospect of higher U.S. interest rates will not buoy the dollar, as dollar buyers are now focusing on investor interest in the U.S. asset market.

Currency analysts said there are fears that Wednesday's U.S. July retail sales data will show strong consumer demand. Reuters is forecasting a 0.7-percent rise in U.S. retail sales overall and an increase of 0.5 percent in sales excluding automobiles.
The Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Sales Index said U.S. seasonally-adjusted retail sales rose 0.9 percent in the week ending August 9.
Traders and analysts said September marks could test resistance at $0.5400, or 1.8550 spot, ahead of the sales data.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000035 at $0.008623, marks were down $0.0011 at $0.5374, Swiss francs were off $0.0006 at $0.6577, sterling was off $0.0128 at $1.5754, Canadian dollars were steady at $0.7191, and Australian dollars were up $0.0003 at $0.7390. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
